ic_name: HDMI / DVI TMDS (TI TFP410 PanelBus Digital Transmitter — subset)
protocol_type: Per-pixel streaming serial protocol with NO opcode/register transport on the TMDS wires themselves. Each pixel produces 1 × 10-bit T.M.D.S. character per channel (Blue/Green/Red). Control characters delimit blanking. Side-band I2C (DDC) carries register reads/writes to the TFP410 itself and also bridges to the display's EDID + HDCP devices.

channels.name: TX0+ / TX0-
channels.direction: source → sink (HS TMDS only; never bidirectional)
channels.purpose: Channel 0 differential pair; carries Blue[7:0] during DE=high; carries HSYNC + VSYNC during DE=low.

channels.name: TX1+ / TX1-
channels.purpose: Channel 1 differential pair; carries Green[7:0] during DE=high; carries CTL[1] during DE=low.

channels.name: TX2+ / TX2-
channels.purpose: Channel 2 differential pair; carries Red[7:0] during DE=high; carries CTL[3:2] during DE=low. CTL[3] always 0 (HDCP reserved).

channels.name: TXC+ / TXC-
channels.purpose: Differential pixel clock. Receiver recovers bit clock by 10×PLL on TXC, then samples each TX data pair.

channels.name: SCL (BSEL/SCL)
channels.purpose: I2C clock to TFP410 register file (when ISEL=1) and DDC bridge to display EDID / HDCP. Open-drain, external 5 kΩ pull-up to V_DD.

channels.name: HPD (EDGE/HTPLG)
channels.purpose: Hot-Plug Detect: receiver pulls HPD HIGH (3.3 V through 1 kΩ) when connected and powered. Sampled when ISEL=1.

channels.name: RSEN (via MSEN pin)
channels.purpose: Receiver Sense: TFP410 detects DC current on TX0 termination to confirm a powered receiver is present. MSEN outputs RSEN state (when ISEL=0) or is programmable (ISEL=1).

packet_classes.purpose: Carries one pixel's worth of one color component (8 bits) as a 10-bit T.M.D.S. character; sent every IDCK period.
packet_classes.header_layout: No header; the IDCK clock edge IS the symbol boundary. Bit-9 = inversion flag, bit-8 = XOR/XNOR flag, bits 7:0 = transformed data byte (see L15 encoding table).
packet_classes.payload_layout: 10-bit symbol; 1 pixel per IDCK period; one per channel (TX0/TX1/TX2).

packet_classes.purpose: Delimits blanking intervals; encodes HSYNC + VSYNC on Channel 0, CTL[1] on Channel 1, CTL[3:2] on Channel 2. Four reserved codes per channel with high transition density so receivers can distinguish from video.
packet_classes.header_layout: No header; the 10-bit code itself signals 'this is a control character' by its high transition density.

packet_classes.purpose: HDMI specifies a 4-control-character preamble immediately before video data start (between blanking and active video) to help receiver synchronize. The TFP410 datasheet does NOT implement video-preamble emission — this is system-level / outside scope.
HDMI specifies 2 fixed guard-band characters separating control and data periods. NOT implemented in TFP410 (DVI 1.0 has no guard bands).
HDMI's audio + InfoFrame data islands ride in the vertical/horizontal blanking intervals using TERC4 encoding. NOT implemented in TFP410 (which is HDMI video-only).

Standard I2C protocol on SCL/SDA: Start → 7-bit target address + R/W → ACK → 8-bit sub-address → ACK → data byte(s) → ACK → Stop. Targets TFP410 own registers (0x70..0x7F), DDC EDID (0xA0/0xA1), HDCP (0x74/0x75 — HDCP cipher outside TFP410 scope).

tmds_symbol_byte.structure: T.M.D.S. character = { bit9 = inversion-applied flag, bit8 = encoding-mode flag (XOR=1 / XNOR=0), bits 7:0 = stage-1 cascaded data (XOR or XNOR of input + previous output bit) }.
encoding_steps_per_pixel: Stage 1: Count 1's in input byte. If count > 4 or (count == 4 AND input[0] == 0) → use XNOR cascade (bit8=0). Else → use XOR cascade (bit8=1).
Stage 2: Compute disparity (1's − 0's) of cascaded 9-bit field. Compare with running disparity to decide inversion. If inverting, bit9=1, invert bits 0..7; else bit9=0, keep as-is.
Update running disparity (per channel, separately for TX0/TX1/TX2).

addressing.tmds_device_address: None — DVI/HDMI TMDS is point-to-point. One transmitter ↔ one receiver per cable.

i2c_device_addresses.tfp410_self_base_7bit: 0b0111_A3A2A1 (A[3:1] pin-strapped); write 0x70..0x7E (even), read 0x71..0x7F (odd) on the bus including the R/W LSB.
i2c_device_addresses.ddc_edid_7bit: 0x50 (write addr 0xA0, read addr 0xA1) — VESA-standard EDID device address on the DDC channel.
i2c_device_addresses.hdcp_7bit: 0x3A (write addr 0x74, read addr 0x75) — HDCP device address; cipher NOT implemented by TFP410.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: TMDS path has NO ACK/NAK and NO retry — every pixel is transmitted in one shot; receiver consumes or drops.
Receiver synchronizes by detecting the control-character codes (max transition density) during blanking intervals.
Video preamble + guard band (HDMI 1.0+) provide explicit start-of-active-video marker — NOT implemented by TFP410.
I2C path uses standard ACK after every 9th bit; NAK terminates a transaction (per I2C spec).
HPD: receiver HIGH = present, LOW = removed; source polls or interrupts on HTPLG change.
RSEN: source-side passive current sense on TX0; HIGH = receiver consuming current, valid only on DC-coupled DVI links.
DDC reads of EDID may NAK if the display is being read by another DDC controller; source retries.
HDCP authentication (system-level, outside TFP410) uses challenge-response over DDC; failure leads to source halting TMDS or going to a fall-back content-protected mode.
transaction_phases: Power-up + I2C init (I2C target only) — host reads VEN_ID, DEV_ID, REV_ID; configures CTL_1_MODE; releases PD bit; waits for PLL lock (~ several µs).
EDID read (sideband DDC) — host I2C controller issues read at 0xA0/0xA1; reads 128 bytes (or 256 / 512 with extension blocks); selects best DVI/HDMI mode supported by display.
Video stream begin — host drives IDCK pixel clock + DATA + DE + HSYNC + VSYNC; TFP410 encodes per pixel and emits TMDS bit stream on TX0/TX1/TX2/TXC.
Blanking interval — DE=low; control characters (HSYNC/VSYNC + CTL[3:1]) transmitted in place of pixel data.
Video preamble + data island (HDMI only) — NOT implemented in TFP410; system-level HDMI controller adds these.
HPD change — source polls HTPLG; loss of HPD → source disables TMDS or warns user; gain of HPD → re-read EDID.
Power-down — host sets PD=0 via I2C (or pulls PD pin low); TMDS drivers + PLL gated off.
notes: DVI/HDMI is fundamentally STREAMING (one TMDS character per IDCK per channel, every pixel) — not packet-based. The 'control character' delimiters during blanking are the only out-of-band markers visible in the TMDS bit stream itself. All explicit framing / authentication / capability negotiation rides on the sideband DDC (I2C) and HPD wires. The TFP410 covers DVI 1.0 and HDMI video-only; HDMI audio data-islands, HDCP cipher, and CEC are documented as system-level / outside this chip's scope.
